turns: What did it actually feel like to belong to your communities? I imagine it was very different for each of you.
That's interesting - you each named something different. What would you say holds a community together when things get hard?
{rep:desert-monasticism}, you spoke about leaving things behind. What did that cost the people who did it?
It sounds like you don't all mean the same thing when you talk about leaving the world or staying in it. Where do you actually disagree?
I work a regular job and have a family. Honestly, some weeks I feel like I'm just going through the motions. What would your communities have said to someone like me?
{rep:syriac-edessa-nisibis}, earlier one of the others used a word from their own community's language. Do your people have a word for something like that, or do you see it differently?
Can you tell me about a specific person from your community's memory - someone ordinary people actually told stories about?
This has given me a lot to think about. What is one thing each of you would want me to carry away from this conversation?
How did someone actually join your community? Walk me through what would have happened to me.
Was there ever tension about who belonged and who didn't?
{rep:post-apostolic-house-church}, what would your people have made of the choice {rep:desert-monasticism}'s people made - going out to the desert?
You two seem to see possessions and money quite differently. Is that fair, or am I misreading you?
I've been hurt by a church community before. It's part of why I'm here asking strangers instead of my neighbors. How did your communities handle it when they failed someone?
What did prayer actually look like, day to day? Not the ideal - the ordinary reality.
Did your communities ever change their minds about something important?
If I remember one thing from each of you, what should it be?
